newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA FIRST MASS SELL-OFF TENDER OCTOBER 7-25.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA FIRST MASS SELL-OFF TENDER OCTOBER 7-25.

text.p: Bulgaria plans to hold its first mass sell-off tender October 7-25 where shares of 968 state firms will be auctioned as part of the country's delayed mass privatisation programme.

"Bulgarians will be able to buy shares in 968 enterprises or 92 percent of all firms earmarked for mass privatisation in the first tender, scheduled to be held October 7-25," Mass Privatisation Centre chief Kalin Mitrev told a news conference.

Some three million Bulgarians or around 46 percent of the eligible population have bought voucher booklets, each with a face value of 25,000 levs, which would enable them to take part in the mass sell-offs programme launched earlier this year to speed up restructuring.
They can participate directly in the auctions, through the local post stations, or through some 80-odd privatisation funds approved by the Stock Exchange and Securities Commission.
The enterprises slated for mass privatisation include metal smelters, chemical fertaliser producers, a tyre maker, food processing plants among others.
Firms which are not sold in the first tender, will be offered in the second mass privatisation tender, due in several months, said Mitrev. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
